title.narrative: Assessment of housing conditions and other socioeconomic determinants of Tubercu

description.narrative: Uganda’s rapid urban population growth has led to the development of densely populated and poorly planned urban slum settlements. The sub-standard living conditions in these areas lead to high levels of ill health, and are particularly conducive to the transmission of TB which is also fuelled by the high prevalence of HIV. Uganda is classified as a high TB burden country but TB is under funded and also under-researched particularly in urban slum settlements. There is a considerable lack of reliable data on TB needs in these slum communities to inform the development of effective strategies to address TB prevention, diagnosis, and treatment programs to tackle the root causes of the spread of TB and its close linkages with HIV/AIDS. In order to address this gap a NA is proposed in 3 urban slum project sites in Uganda to map services and gaps, analyse facility level data on TB incidence and explore socio-economic factors affecting its spread. The approach employed will have a strong community empowerment focus, working to build capacity and motivation amongst community members to take control of and address their own health needs. The proposed research sites differ significantly, lending interesting comparisons to the NA.
